events.description: Senate Committee on Indian Affairs hearing as part of Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States; witnesses including Mr. Couro, J. A. Moore, Capt. V. J. La Chusa, and Mr. Dady testified
Annual Indian fiesta held August 3-6, 1933; site of confrontation between US Indian police under Moore and Mission Indian Federation police

events.type: Confrontation between US Indian police and federation Indians
events.description: Approximately 75-100 Indians surrounded Moore and demanded he and US Indian police leave the fiesta, threatening violence; Moore reported some federation police carried concealed weapons
Meeting held in federation meeting house at 6 p.m. Saturday; Willis and Prather present; first part open, last part closed to federation members only; William Pablo discovered listening outside
J. A. Moore sent telegram to Commissioner Collier reporting near-conflict at Mesa Grande fiesta and requesting firm backing from Washington

Collier responded authorizing Moore to attend fiesta, observe, and leave physical interference with liquor to federation police; warned that federation's actions jeopardized future recognition by US Government

events.type: Reading of Collier telegram to Mesa Grande Indians
events.description: Moore returned to Mesa Grande and read Collier's responding telegram to assembled Indians, which averted further trouble and silenced ringleaders

events.type: Moore's detailed report to Commissioner Collier
events.description: J. A. Moore submitted detailed written report of Mesa Grande fiesta activities August 3-6 to Commissioner Collier

events.type: Muskogee conference with Five Civilized Tribes
events.description: Conference held with Indians of Five Civilized Tribes of Oklahoma; Collier made statements about his and Ickes's appointments
Robert Magee, ex-US Indian Service policeman, submitted affidavit contesting Moore's report, swearing no armed federation police were encountered and fiesta was peaceful
Grace La Chusa submitted statement disputing Moore's telegram account of the Mesa Grande fiesta incident

events.type: Letter from Mesa Grande committee to John Collier
events.description: Letter signed by V. J. La Chusa, George Ponchetti, Remijo L. Chusa, Reinaldo Duro, and Frank Loan disputing Moore's account of the Mesa Grande fiesta

events.type: Letter from Moore to A. A. Grisold
events.description: Moore responded to September 8 letter requesting names of Indians carrying concealed weapons at Mesa Grande fiesta; reported memorandum with names had been lost
Prior incident of shooting and killing at Campo reservation referenced by Moore as precedent for danger at Mesa Grande
Earlier Senate investigation that included the Campo case and examined employee conduct under Agent Ellis
Robert Magee discharged from US Indian Service for inefficiency, specifically for not performing duty and not carrying out specific assigned missions

legislative_actions.outcome: Debated; caused dissension among Indians according to Mr. Couro; Chairman defended bill as beneficial to Indians giving them more power over their affairs than ever before

testimony.witness_title: California Indian community member and voter
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States
testimony.subject: Complaints about Commissioner John Collier, the Wheeler Bill, employee retention under Dady, and conduct of Indian police
testimony.key_claims: Commissioner Collier has caused more dissension and dissatisfaction among Indians than any previous Commissioner; the Wheeler Bill was setting Indians back 100 years instead of advancing them; same employees remain from the Ellis era who mistreated Indians; Indian police are retained indefinitely without accountability; J. A. Moore sent a telegram to Collier about federation police carrying guns at Mesa Grande but would not show the telegram to Indians when asked; requested changes in the police force; stated he is a voter and citizen and wishes to continue as such; referenced Muskogee hearing page 20 where Collier stated he and Ickes were not appointed politically; stated Collier asked for Indian endorsement while his appointment was held up by Senator McAdoo

testimony.witness_title: Special Officer, United States Indian Service
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande fiesta incident of August 1933; telegram to Commissioner Collier; concealed weapons
testimony.key_claims: A telegram was sent about trouble at Mesa Grande fiesta; some federation police carried concealed weapons which he personally witnessed; Robert Magee was present at the fiesta but did not operate as an officer and was later discharged for inefficiency; no formal written charges had been preferred against John Lewis; Moore's authority comes from Washington and he has no connection to Mr. Dady
testimony.questioner: The Chairman; Senator Thomas; Mr. Couro

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States
testimony.subject: Disputing Moore's claim that federation police were armed at Mesa Grande fiesta
testimony.key_claims: Moore is mistaken about federation police being armed; federation police are not allowed to carry any arms; Indians are peaceful people who do not need arms; Moore's report said several federation police were armed but he should name which ones; federation police carry nothing for protection, not even a club

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States
testimony.subject: John Lewis as Indian policeman; police force management
testimony.key_claims: John Lewis is as far as he knows a good policeman; Winslow is making a complaint against John Lewis; Mr. Moore is in charge of the police

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States
testimony.subject: Disputing Moore's account of armed federation police at Mesa Grande fiesta August 5, 1933
testimony.key_claims: On the night of August 5, 1933, under Moore's leadership, no armed Indian Federation policemen were encountered; not one arrest was made; the fiesta went on very peacefully; Moore's report is not true; on many occasions Mission Indian Federation police were helpful rather than a disturbance
testimony.questioner: N/A (affidavit read into record by Mr. Couro)
